doc.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998

title: Opening and introduction by Monk Rowe
summary: Rowe introduces Conniff and the 'Ray Conniff sound' and asks if he would do it all again.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: We are filming in San Diego for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. And I am honored to have Mr. Ray Conniff with me — trombonist and arranger and composer. And I want to tell you that when I grew up, in the 50s, I lived outside Rochester, New York, and it was kind of a typical suburban home, and in my house, my parents played Glenn Miller and a little Basie, and a lot of Ray Conniff. So it’s a real pleasure for me to be talking with you today, because your sound is something that was present a lot as I grew up. I think probably it’s a pretty huge compliment to have people refer to “a sound,” you know, like “well what we need is that Ray Conniff sound.” And it’s been a long road, but would you do it all again?
Would you do it all again?
